chapters.title: SURFACE, NOT JUST SHAPE
chapters.speech: An electrospun polymer mat can have the intended shape and still invite bacterial colonization. This study asked whether its surface could be changed.

chapters.title: THREE REAL STEPS
chapters.speech: The published method combined electrospinning, radiofrequency plasma treatment, and then ascorbic or fumaric acid modification. This is the original figure from that experiment.

chapters.title: THIRTY SECONDS
chapters.speech: Plasma treatment produced reactive surfaces. The study selected thirty seconds for subsequent modification, balancing functionalization with damage that can accumulate during longer treatment.

chapters.title: THE ACTUAL MICROGRAPHS
chapters.speech: These micrographs belong to this exact scaffold paper. Untreated, plasma-treated, ascorbic-grafted and fumaric-grafted fibres show different surface textures, with three-micrometre scale bars.

chapters.title: WETTABILITY IS NOT SIMPLE
chapters.speech: Water contact angle fell with plasma treatment and ascorbic grafting. Fumaric acid grafting instead produced a high water contact angle. The measured table shows why material identity matters.

chapters.title: A CHEMICAL FINGERPRINT
chapters.speech: The paper's infrared spectra support interpretation of functional changes after treatment. Spectral assignments belong alongside microscopy and the other material evidence, not in place of them.

chapters.title: THE ANTIMICROBIAL ASSAY
chapters.speech: In the reported colony assessment, both acid-grafted scaffolds received zero growth scores against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. That is an in-vitro result.

chapters.title: NOT YET A CLINICAL DEVICE
chapters.speech: The research demonstrates surface alteration and an antimicrobial response in an assay. Clinical infection prevention, durability and biological compatibility remain separate questions.
